senses.definition: bitterness and ill feeling, especially in speech or debate
senses.example: The partnership ended in acrimony, with each side blaming the other.

senses.definition: something that belongs to a different time period than the one in which it appears
senses.example: A wristwatch on a Roman soldier is a glaring anachronism.

senses.definition: severe or strict in manner or attitude
senses.example: The austere headmaster rarely smiled.

senses.definition: plain and without decoration or comfort
senses.example: The cabin was austere: a bed, a table and a wood stove.

senses.definition: truthful and straightforward; frank
senses.example: In a candid interview, the coach admitted the team had played badly.

senses.definition: secret cooperation in order to cheat or deceive others
senses.example: The two firms were fined for collusion in fixing prices.

senses.definition: causing harm or damage
senses.example: Smoking has a deleterious effect on nearly every organ.

senses.definition: modest or shy because of a lack of self-confidence
senses.example: The diffident student rarely spoke unless called on.

senses.definition: having or showing care and effort in one's work or duties
senses.example: A diligent researcher, she checked every source twice.

senses.definition: the feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's respect
senses.example: She looked at the cheap souvenirs with disdain.

senses.definition: to consider unworthy of one's respect or consideration
senses.example: He disdained any job that required wearing a tie.

senses.definition: to spread something, especially information, widely
senses.example: The health department disseminated leaflets about the vaccine.

senses.definition: a lack of harmony among musical notes
senses.example: The composer used dissonance to build tension.

senses.definition: a tension or clash between two things that don't fit together
senses.example: There was a dissonance between his warm words and cold actions.

senses.definition: tending to be different or to develop in different directions
senses.example: The two scientists reached divergent conclusions from the same data.

senses.definition: inclined to lay down principles as undeniably true, without considering evidence or other opinions
senses.example: His dogmatic insistence on one method frustrated the team.

senses.definition: hesitating or doubting
senses.example: She was dubious about the plan from the start.

senses.definition: not to be relied on; suspect
senses.example: The claim came from a dubious source.

senses.definition: difficult to find, catch or achieve
senses.example: Success remained elusive despite years of effort.

senses.definition: irrelevant or unrelated to the subject being dealt with
senses.example: Cut any extraneous details from your essay.

senses.definition: lacking significance through having been overused; unoriginal and trite
senses.example: The plot relies on a hackneyed twist about a long-lost twin.

senses.definition: to hinder or impede the movement or progress of
senses.example: Heavy snow hampered the rescue effort.

senses.definition: treating all rivals or disputants equally; fair and just
senses.example: Judges must be impartial.

senses.definition: unable to be appeased or placated
senses.example: He was an implacable enemy of the new law.

senses.definition: not in harmony or keeping with the surroundings or other aspects of something
senses.example: A neon sign looked incongruous on the medieval street.

senses.definition: having or showing no skill; clumsy
senses.example: The inept handling of the crisis cost the minister her job.

senses.definition: lacking the ability or strength to move; motionless
senses.example: The patient lay inert on the stretcher.

senses.definition: chemically inactive
senses.example: Helium is an inert gas.

senses.definition: hard to control or deal with
senses.example: Homelessness has proved an intractable problem for the city.

senses.definition: to mourn a person's loss or death; to express regret or disappointment about something
senses.example: Fans lamented the closing of the old cinema.

senses.definition: a passionate expression of grief or sorrow
senses.example: The song is a lament for a lost homeland.

senses.definition: expressed clearly; easy to understand
senses.example: The textbook offers a lucid explanation of genetics.

senses.definition: thinking clearly, especially in the intervals of an illness
senses.example: He had lucid moments when he recognized his family.

senses.definition: very generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival or someone less powerful
senses.example: The champion was magnanimous in victory, praising her opponent.

senses.definition: having or showing a wish to do evil to others
senses.example: The villain's malevolent grin sent a shiver through the audience.

senses.definition: stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action
senses.example: The obdurate official would not waive the fee.

senses.definition: not able to be seen through; not transparent
senses.example: The bathroom window is made of opaque glass.

senses.definition: hard or impossible to understand
senses.example: The regulations are written in opaque legal language.

senses.definition: a seemingly absurd or contradictory statement that may nevertheless prove true
senses.example: It is a paradox that the more choices we have, the less satisfied we often feel.

senses.definition: carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection
senses.example: The guard gave our passports a perfunctory glance.

senses.definition: having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way
senses.example: Rumors had a pernicious effect on morale.

senses.definition: to make something, typically an undesirable situation or belief, continue indefinitely
senses.example: The textbook perpetuates old myths about the region.

senses.definition: spreading widely throughout an area or group of people
senses.example: The smell of smoke was pervasive after the fire.

senses.definition: devoutly religious
senses.example: The pious old woman went to church every morning.

senses.definition: making a hypocritical display of virtue
senses.example: Spare us your pious lectures about honesty.

senses.definition: dealing with things sensibly and realistically, based on practical considerations
senses.example: We need a pragmatic solution, not a perfect one.

senses.definition: an inclination or natural tendency to behave in a particular way
senses.example: He has a propensity to exaggerate.

senses.definition: bitterness or resentfulness, especially when long-standing
senses.example: They settled the dispute without rancor.

senses.definition: not or no longer needed or useful; superfluous
senses.example: Remove the redundant words from the sentence.

senses.definition: to prove a statement or theory to be wrong or false
senses.example: The scientist refuted the claim with new data.

senses.definition: able to recover quickly from difficult conditions
senses.example: Children are often more resilient than adults expect.

senses.definition: (of a material) able to spring back into shape after bending or stretching
senses.example: The running track is made of a resilient rubber.

senses.definition: not easily convinced; having doubts or reservations
senses.example: Scientists were skeptical of the miracle cure.

senses.definition: tending to keep a firm hold of something; persistent
senses.example: The tenacious reporter followed the story for years.

senses.definition: not certain or fixed; provisional
senses.example: We made tentative plans to meet in June.

senses.definition: done without confidence; hesitant
senses.example: The toddler took a few tentative steps.

senses.definition: lasting only for a short time; impermanent
senses.example: The pain was transient and soon passed.

senses.definition: staying or working in a place for only a short time
senses.example: The town has a large transient population of seasonal workers.

senses.definition: (of a position or view) not able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection
senses.example: After the scandal, his position as treasurer became untenable.

senses.definition: to speak or write about in an abusively disparaging manner
senses.example: The press vilified the coach after the loss.

senses.definition: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
senses.example: The stock market has been volatile this month.

senses.definition: (of a person) liable to display rapid changes of emotion
senses.example: He had a volatile temper and often shouted at his staff.

senses.definition: having or showing great energy or enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective
senses.example: The zealous volunteers knocked on every door in the district.
